title: Fix role-binding shadowing when Private SAML assertions are revalidated during KMS key rotation
creator: Priya Anand
description:
Summary:
Several enterprise Private customers reported intermittent authorization changes after scheduled KMS envelope rotations. In the failure window, SAML assertions arriving at the private control plane were accepted but the parsed role claim was occasionally ignored, causing role-binding shadowing where a default fallback role (viewer) was applied to requests that should have been allowed or denied based on the assertion. Audit entries for those authorization decisions were also missing in some tenants due to an unexpected tenant-id normalization edge case in the audit writer.

Root cause hypothesis: the assertion validation path re-fetches verification keys from the KMS key cache during envelope rotation. A race condition combined with a brittle JSON parsing branch caused the 'roles' attribute to be treated as opaque (dropped) when the assertion revalidation used the transient key path. Separately, the audit writer relied on a best-effort tenant header which was briefly unset for a sub-path, leading to audit writes being routed to a no-op buffer (supressed).

Impact:
- Affected customers: 3 large Private customers (reported).
- Behavior: intermittent loss of role claims for 10-30s during rotation; some requests fell back to viewer or failed authorization.
- Severity: P0 (customer escalations, potential security posture regression).

Acceptance criteria / success metric:
- No regression during KMS rotations in canary test (simulated rotations every 30s for 1 hour).
- Role claim must be preserved and validated across key swap path with deterministic semantics.
- Audit events emitted for every auth decision; no more suppressed audit entries during rotation.
- Hotfix deployed to Private control plane with canary and rollout plan; customers notified and mitigation steps documented.

Proposed fix (high level):
1) Add an atomic key-swap mechanism in the KMS verification cache: new verification key replaces old only after full population of the derived lookup structure.
2) Short-circuit the revalidation branch: if initial signature validation succeeds, avoid an additional parse/normalize step that can drop the 'roles' attribute; instead validate signature then parse claims exactly once using a safe JSON path.
3) Harden audit writer tenant resolution: fall back to explicit tenant claim from SAML assertion if header absent and log a deterministic warning (not supress).
4) Backfill missing audit events by replaying stored request metadata for the affected time windows for impacted tenants.
5) Add unit + integration tests that simulate rotating keys and assert that role claims and audit events persist.

Engineering tasks (this ticket):
- Implement atomic cache swap and parse-path fix (ENG).
- Add tests and CI gating for simulated KMS rotation.
- Prepare migration/backfill script for audit logs and coordinate with Data team.
- Create canary / rollout plan for Private control plane and communicate to customers.

Documentation / comms:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/ENG-25342+priv-kms-rotation-audit-backfill (draft)
- Customer tickets: CS-12489, CS-12492, CS-12495 (escalations linked)
- Support runbook updated: https://drive.redwood.ai/Support/priv-saml-kms-issue-runbook.md

- Backfill job draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pull/214 (audit-backfill)
